text: There is a pit ahead. It has acid in it. Fortunately, I have opened a doorway across it.
I have opened a doorway for you. I am told it is customary to walk through doorways.
Step into the blue one. It is the one that is not in the acid.
The blue button on your gun puts a portal on a white panel. I would not overthink it.
One end is mine. The other end is yours. You are holding the tool for it.
There is one white panel on this side. Put a portal on it, and find out where it leads.
No doorway this time. Both portals are yours. I have taken the liberty of removing nearly every white surface on the other side of that wall.
You can put a portal on anything you can see. That is the entire technique.
You can put a portal on anything you can see. Anything. Glass has never stopped anybody looking.
There is one white surface past that wall. You will have to look through something to find it.
The cube cannot walk. You can. One of you will have to carry the other.
You can get into the cube's room by portal. The cube can leave it the same way, if somebody is holding it.
I have opened a portal in the floor. Where the other end goes is your department.
The cube does not need you to come with it. It can fall perfectly well on its own.
The cell has a ceiling. Ceilings, in this building, are sometimes white.
Speed is the one thing a portal never takes from you. I find that generous of it.
Speed in is speed out. I did not make the rule. I merely enforce it.
Falling is the fastest thing you do in here. Fall into something, and come out somewhere useful.
You leave a portal the way it faces. Make one face up, and fall into the other.
The cube is coming with you. It has no say in the matter. Neither, really, do you.
You can hold the cube while you fall. It will not let go first.
A beam goes into one portal and out of the other, and leaves the way that portal faces.
Two receivers. One beam. They do not both need it at the same time.
They only see what is in front of them. I consider that their one flaw. Do not be shot.
They only see what is in front of them, and only so far.
Pillars hide you, and your health comes back behind them. The far wall is further from both of them than it looks.
The door is on the other side of that wall. So is the sentry.
It wakes facing the way you faced when you put it down. A wall is very poor company. That is the point.
There are two pads. One of them lands next to where the crate needs to be. The crate does not need you to ride with it.
Carry a portal through a reset field and it closes. A portal shot, however, goes straight through.
The cube cannot go through the field. Nothing says it has to.
The camera is the weight. It just does not know it yet.
Cameras hang on walls. Walls, in here, can be made to stop holding things.
Inside the pen, loose things fall up. You do not. I made sure.
Things that fall up keep going until something stops them. A portal counts as something.
There is a second sentry in a cell over there, facing the wall. It is in disgrace.
A sleeping sentry blocks the view of a waking one. The cell has a window, and a white panel behind it.
They are bolted to the floor, so do not get ideas. The button is up on the ledge with the door. It wants something heavy.
Each of them would shoot the other on sight. All they lack is a view. You have the portals.
The door also wants the crate on its plate. The plate is through the tunnel.
Fetch the crate before you aim the light. Otherwise you will be fetching it through the same portal twice.
The crate's panel faces away from you. That portal can only be set from the other side of the field.
A crate on the plate in the niche is a crate in the sentry's window.
Give it a portal to look into, and put the other one behind it.
The crate can fall up into one ceiling portal and out of the other. Preferably the one past the field.
The crate is coming with you. How it travels is up to you.
Drop the crate into the floor under the gantry first. It leaves the back wall faster than a sentry likes.
The higher the portal you fall out of, the further you fly. Use all of the strip.
Both nozzles drip on the floor by the door, where they can do no harm. Try them.
Paste goes through portals at the speed it fell. Send the pink across. Put the green where you will need a way up.
Put a portal on the square where the pad drops you. The fall that follows can come out somewhere else.
The panel by the door can only be seen when all three presses are up. Wait for that before you touch the switch.
Set every portal you need before you step off the amber plate. The three seconds are for walking, not shooting.
The panel's portal is only useful while it is over the gantry. Time your step for that, both ways.
This pit is thirty four metres long. Nothing in here can throw you that far.
A floor portal under a ceiling portal makes a fall that never stops. Once it is fast enough, move the exit.
Each next panel can only be seen from the end of the walkway before it. Stand on the light, and aim it again.
Send the crate up first. Then follow it, and look around from where it went.
Your first primed board decides what you can see next. Pick the one that looks at the most bare board.
Open the way up before you step off the second slow button. After that, you will only have three seconds.
The cell's one panel does two jobs. The crate goes in through it first, then the light. The sentry will have to move first.
The hatch is not the only way onto the float. The booth faces somewhere much more restful.
The crate leaves the cell through the panel on the inside of its wall, not through the doorway. Only send the light after that.
Crate on the pad first. Something is standing where the pad lands you.
The far sentry can see the near one, given the right two walls. After that, look for a panel you could not see before.
Put both portals up while the inner door is open. Then go and get the crate.
Only a burned-out sentry comes off its bolts. The beam can do the burning, from the short panel on the other wall.
The door wants the crate.
A crate dropped from the ceiling onto a sentry knocks it over. The same crate can do it twice.
Flip gravity and the loose two fall up, then come down hard. The bolted one needs a crate from above.
The crate goes round the field by portal first, to lift the shutter. Then send the spark, and catch it from the far side.
Knock both cameras down. One goes over on the pad. The other one goes with you.
Light first. Everything else in here waits on it.
The far sentry can be shown itself. A camera comes down when its wall opens beside it.
Cube first. The light can wait. It always has.
The pad will fly the cube over the pit. The field it can only cross by portal.
